title: Daily Security Intelligence Briefing — September 18, 2026
summary: Cloud permanent data loss disclosures following physical attacks in the Middle East and zero-click AI agent supply chain flaws top today's threat landscape. (Help Net Security, The Hacker News)

tier1.title: 1. AWS Confirms Permanent Data Loss in Middle East Regions Following Drone Strikes

fields.label: Source & Article Link
fields.value: Help Net Security

fields.label: Technical Severity / Domain
fields.value: Cloud Infrastructure / Data Destruction (Critical)

fields.label: Why You Must Read This
fields.value: Amazon Web Services (AWS) officially acknowledged the permanent loss of customer data and resources stored in its Middle East (Bahrain) me-south-1 region and an availability zone in the UAE following physical drone strikes. The confirmation highlights severe resilience vulnerabilities for organizations relying on single-region cloud hosting in volatile geopolitical zones. The inability to recover these workloads forces an immediate shift toward mandatory multi-region redundancy and off-cloud data backup practices for global cloud infrastructure.

fields.label: Recommended Immediate Action
fields.value: Audit all cloud deployments in high-risk regions and immediately implement cross-region or multi-cloud asynchronous data replication and backups.

tier1.title: 2. Zero-Click 'Plugin4Shell' Flaw Exposes Four Major AI Coding Agents to RCE

fields.label: Source & Article Link
fields.value: The Hacker News

fields.label: Technical Severity / Domain
fields.value: AI Supply Chain / Zero-Click RCE (Critical)

fields.label: Why You Must Read This
fields.value: Security firm Air Security disclosed 'Plugin4Shell', a zero-click remote code execution flaw impacting Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, GitHub Copilot, and Gemini CLI. The vulnerability allows repository owners to secretly swap pinned plugin code with malicious payloads, bypassing explicit version locks during agent execution. Unpatched instances allow attackers full execution privileges on developer workstations running these AI coding tools.

fields.label: Recommended Immediate Action
fields.value: Immediately update Claude Code to v2.1.179+ and OpenAI Codex to v0.146.0+, and disable unverified third-party plugin repositories across engineering environments.

tier2.title: 1. Check Point Fixes Critical Management Server Flaw Granting Root Access

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Vulnerability Management

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: Check Point has issued emergency security updates to address a critical vulnerability in its Security Management and Log Servers. The flaw allows unauthenticated remote attackers to execute arbitrary code with root privileges over the network.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Unauthenticated network attackers can achieve full root execution on core management servers.; Check Point released emergency patches via its LivePatch automatic update mechanism.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: A critical vulnerability in Check Point's Security Management and Log Servers could allow an attacker without login credentials to run code as root on those servers over the network.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: The Hacker News

tier2.title: 2. Critical Unbound DNSSEC Heap Overflow Allows Remote Code Execution

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Infrastructure & Core Protocols

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: NLnet Labs released Unbound 1.26.1 to address a critical heap overflow vulnerability (CVE-2026-81642) within its DNSSEC validator component. An attacker controlling a malicious DNS zone can craft responses that trigger the overflow and execute arbitrary code on vulnerable resolvers.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Impacts all versions of the Unbound DNS resolver prior to version 1.26.1.; Exploitation requires no authentication and triggers when a resolver queries a controlled malicious zone.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: An attacker who controls a malicious zone and queries a vulnerable resolver can trigger it, enabling remote code execution.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: The Hacker News

tier2.title: 3. Brevo Supply-Chain Attack Injected ClickFix Scripts via Stolen Cloudflare Key

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Supply Chain Security

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: Email marketing vendor Brevo confirmed a supply-chain breach after threat actors compromised a Cloudflare API key. The attackers used the API key to inject malicious ClickFix social-engineering scripts into Brevo's web assets and embedded customer JavaScript files.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Attackers leveraged a stolen Cloudflare API key to modify public-facing JavaScript assets.; Injected scripts delivered ClickFix popups prompting users to copy-paste malicious terminal commands.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: Brevo confirmed that attackers stole a Cloudflare API key and used it to inject malicious ClickFix scripts into its websites and JavaScript files embedded on customer sites.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: BleepingComputer

tier2.title: 4. Critical Docker Sandboxes Escape Exposes macOS Host File Systems

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Container & Virtualization Security

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: Docker warned of a critical security vulnerability (CVE-2026-77179) in Docker Sandboxes on macOS. The bug enables malicious code running within a guest virtual machine to break out of isolated directories and manipulate host files.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Guest code inside Docker Sandboxes VM can escape isolation to read or modify arbitrary host files.; Exploits execute with the full privileges of the macOS user account running the VM.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: Malicious code running inside a Docker Sandboxes virtual machine on macOS could escape the project directory shared into it and read or change files anywhere else on the host.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: The Hacker News

tier2.title: 5. CISA Issues Guidance Urging Cyber Decoy Deployment for Critical Infrastructure

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Threat Detection & Response

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: CISA published operational guidance recommending that critical infrastructure facilities deploy cyber decoys inside internal networks. The initiative aims to help security teams catch attackers using stolen valid credentials and living-off-the-land techniques.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Decoys provide high-fidelity alerts against lateral movement and unauthorized credential usage.; Guidance aims to make deception technology accessible to smaller, resource-limited security teams.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: The core problem CISA is attempting to address is that many organizations are incapable of detecting adversaries who use legitimate credentials.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: Help Net Security
